articles.title: Good Night At Last
articles.summary: After a long winter with limited stargazing opportunities, astronomers at Fremont Peak experienced exceptionally dark and transparent skies on June 26-27, 1998. The rare conditions, attributed to coastal fog, allowed for easy naked-eye viewing of objects like the North American Nebula, much to the relief of South Bay astronomers.

articles.title: Net Delivery Of Ephemeris
articles.summary: The delivery of the Ephemeris has been consistently delayed in recent months due to inefficiencies at the post office, with no expected improvement in bulk mail service. As an immediate, albeit temporary, solution, the Ephemeris will be published earlier, necessitating earlier deadlines and resulting in older news content, though this is not seen as a long-term fix.

articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: The SJAA Activities Calendar outlines a series of events for August and September, including multiple star parties at various locations like Houge Park, Fremont Peak, and Coe. It also features general meetings with guest speakers, beginning astronomy classes covering topics like planetary observing and astrophotography, and a special equipment night. Members are reminded about SJAA insurance coverage for sponsored events.

articles.title: Rima Brayley
articles.summary: On July 4th, a group of experienced lunar observers (selenists) gathered at Fremont Peak with a variety of telescopes, ranging from 80mm refractors to a 30-inch Challenger scope. Their objective was to determine the minimum aperture required to clearly observe Rima Brayley, a narrow lunar rille described as challenging for small telescopes. Despite the diverse equipment, the author noted they were unable to view the entire Rima Brayley at once in any of the instruments.

articles.title: On Looking Hard:
articles.summary: Observing celestial objects, especially at the limit of a telescope, is a demanding skill that goes beyond simply spotting objects. It requires precise knowledge of where to look, proper dark adaptation, and employing specific techniques. The author emphasizes that effective "looking" is a learnable skill, cultivated through extensive knowledge, practice, and experience.

articles.title: On Small Apertures and Deep Sky:
articles.summary: The author is nearing completion of a Messier survey using a 55mm Vixen refractor and plans to embark on a new observing challenge: the Herschel 400 list with the same small-aperture instrument. While not expecting new vistas, the project aims to be enjoyable, convenient for star parties, and potentially inspire others to pursue deep-sky observing with small telescopes.

articles.title: On high-power eyepieces:
articles.summary: This article provides advice on using high-power eyepieces, suggesting a stepwise increase in magnification until benefits cease due to factors like poor atmospheric seeing, equipment instability, or optical limitations. It recommends using magnifications between one and two times the telescope's clear aperture in millimeters under ideal conditions for optimal detail.

articles.title: On "Averted Imagination":
articles.summary: This brief piece humorously introduces "Averted Imagination" as a necessary technique for observing the fictional "elusive Elvis Nebula." It also notes the need for a specialized "sidereal drive" tracking at the "King rate" to successfully locate this celestial object.

articles.title: Editor's Extras
articles.summary: This 'Editor's Extras' column provides updates on various club activities and schedule changes. It announces an early September general meeting on August 29th, details a Beginning Astronomy Class on August 1st led by Rich Neuschater, and mentions the potential relocation of the club's C-11 PowerStar telescope to Fremont Peak. Additionally, it encourages members to donate old astronomy publications for new enthusiasts at star parties.

articles.title: Ephemeris, continued from Page 1.
articles.summary: This article outlines the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) plan to transition the delivery of their 'Ephemeris' publication from standard mail to a multi-modal approach including First Class Mail, web access, and email. The primary goal is to encourage members to switch to electronic versions to reduce mailing costs, which would then make First Class Mail feasible for remaining paper subscribers. Members are encouraged to opt-out of paper copies if they primarily use the web version, but those who prefer paper will continue to receive it.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for August, detailing optimal times to view various lunar features like specific rilles and Mare Orientale, with prime opportunities highlighted in early August and around the 18th for morning observers. It also notes a close approach between Saturn and the Moon on the 19th. The author includes a recap of a successful July observation of the Orientale Basin and encourages readers to share their own viewing experiences.

articles.title: Akkana Peck
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for the month, detailing the visibility of various planets. Mercury, Venus, and Mars are difficult to spot in the morning twilight, while Jupiter will be visible all night, with a linked tool for satellite predictions. Saturn's rings are well-tilted for viewing, and Uranus and Neptune are near opposition but remain low in the sky.

articles.title: Perseid Meteor Shower
articles.summary: The Perseid Meteor Shower is the year's most popular due to its high rates and favorable August weather in the Northern Hemisphere. While its peak activity is around August 11-13, the 1998 shower will be affected by a full moon, requiring specific viewing directions to observe its bright meteors and their long-lasting trains.

articles.title: Goodnight, continued from Page 1.
articles.summary: This article compiles several amateur astronomers' positive experiences during recent observing nights, primarily on June 26th and the following Saturday. Despite initial concerns about widespread fog, many observers at locations such as Fremont Peak, Mount Tamalpais, and Henry W. Coe State Park reported excellent seeing conditions, clear skies, and significantly reduced light pollution due to an inversion layer that kept fog in the valleys below. Participants consistently noted the unusually warm, dry, and steady air, with some achieving a limiting magnitude of 6.7.

articles.title: Brayley, continued from Page 1.
articles.summary: The article details a lunar observing session at Fremont Peak where amateur astronomers attempted to locate Rima Brayley. Observers used various telescopes, with larger instruments like a 30-inch showing more consistent hints of the elusive rille, though seeing conditions often made observations difficult and uncertain. Several participants shared their differing experiences, highlighting the challenge of confirming this specific lunar feature.

articles.title: Activities Through Other Clubs
articles.summary: This article outlines ongoing astronomical activities hosted by other clubs, encouraging participation from SJAA members. TAC has reserved the Montebello site every Wednesday indefinitely for members, requiring a permit holder. PAS opens Foothill Observatory for public viewing every clear Friday evening with various telescopes and offers solar viewing every clear Saturday morning.

articles.title: August
articles.summary: This document outlines two meetings scheduled for August for the PAS organization. On August 14th, a General Meeting at Foothill College will feature Chuck Vaughn presenting on "Photoshop Enhancement of Astronomical Images." A Board Meeting is also planned for August 19th at the Foothill College Observatory.

articles.title: September
articles.summary: The Palo Alto Astronomical Society (PAS) has scheduled its General Meeting on September 11th and a Board Meeting on September 19th, both at Foothill College. Additionally, a Foothill Park star party is planned for Saturday, August 29th, where telescope owners gain free park access, with setup on Vista Hill and specific parking instructions for participants.

articles.title: AANC Autumn Astronomy Day
articles.summary: The Astronomical Association of Northern California (AANC) is organizing the first "Autumn Astronomy Day" on September 26, 1998, inviting astronomy clubs nationwide to participate. The event aims to provide an alternative opportunity to celebrate astronomy and engage the public, especially after spring weather challenges and to connect with schools early in the academic year. Clubs can schedule their own events or incorporate them into existing programs.

articles.title: Lunar time
articles.summary: This document presents a schedule of key lunar phases, including Full Moon, Last Quarter, New Moon, and First Quarter, for a specific period. It details the precise date, time in PDT, and the corresponding moonrise, transit, and moonset times for each phase.

articles.title: Mercury
articles.summary: This document provides an ephemeris for the planet Mercury, detailing its distance, apparent magnitude, and daily rise, transit, and set times for three specific dates. It also includes the planet's right ascension and declination for those dates, aiding in its celestial localization.

articles.title: Venus
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical ephemeris data for the planet Venus across three dates within a month. It includes details such as its distance from Earth, apparent magnitude, rise, transit, and set times, as well as its Right Ascension and Declination coordinates. This data is useful for tracking Venus's position in the sky.

articles.title: Mars
articles.summary: This document provides a concise ephemeris for Mars across three dates (07, 17, 27), detailing its distance, magnitude, rise, transit, and set times, along with its Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec). It serves as a navigational guide for locating and observing Mars during this period.

articles.title: Jupiter
articles.summary: This document provides astronomical data for Jupiter for three specific dates (7th, 17th, and 27th), including its distance, magnitude, rise, transit, and set times, along with its Right Ascension and Declination. This ephemeris data is useful for observers tracking the giant planet's position in the night sky.

articles.title: Saturn
articles.summary: This document provides current astronomical data for Saturn, including its distance, apparent magnitude, and an ephemeris for three specific dates (07, 17, 27). The ephemeris lists rise, transit, and set times, along with its Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec), serving as a guide for observers.

articles.title: SOL Type G2V Intelligent Life in System ?
articles.summary: This document presents astronomical ephemeris data, including tables detailing "Hours of Darkness," "Astronomical Twilight," and "Sidereal Time" for various dates in August 1997. It also provides specific observing conditions for the "Darkest Saturday Night" of August 22, 1997, listing sunset, twilight, moonset, and dawn times. The content is part of an SJAA Ephemeris from August 1998, providing practical data for stargazers, despite its provocative title.

articles.title: Don Machholz
articles.summary: The article reports on recent comet discoveries by projects such as Linear, Spacewatch, and SOHO (despite a temporary loss of contact with the satellite). It also celebrates the 20th anniversary of Don Machholz's "Comet Comments" newsletter, reflecting on his first comet discovery and the origin of the Messier Marathon. Additionally, it details the Edgar Wilson Award, an annual cash prize for amateur comet discoverers, outlining its criteria and potential payouts.

articles.title: Ephemerides -- Epoch 2000, 0h UTC
articles.summary: This document provides ephemerides for three comets: C/1997 J2 (Meunier-Dupouy), C/1995 O1 (Hale-Bopp), and C/1997 N1 (Tabur), set to Epoch 2000, 0h UTC. For each comet, tables list its Right Ascension, Declination, elongation from the Sun, sky visibility (Morning/Evening), and estimated visual magnitude. This data, spanning from August 5th to September 14th, is crucial for astronomers and observers tracking these celestial objects.

articles.title: Orbital Elements -- Epoch 2000.0
articles.summary: This document provides a table of orbital elements for three comets (Hale-Bopp, Meunier-Dupouy, and Linear), all referenced to Epoch 2000.0. The data includes perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, orbital period, and absolute magnitude. It appears to be a technical reference page from an ephemeris.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current Officers and Board of Directors for an organization. It provides the title, name, and contact phone number for each individual, including the President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer, and several Directors.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: This document lists the staff members and their respective roles for an organization, likely an amateur astronomy club or a related publication called 'Ephemeris'. It includes contacts for editorial, circulation, proofing, printing, and various astronomical programs such as mentoring, observational astronomy, observatory committee, school star parties, and a telescope loaner program.

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) is encouraging its members to submit articles for publication in their newsletter, the SJAA Ephemeris. Members interested in contributing should send their articles via email to Dave North at Timocharis@aol.com.

articles.title: Finding Fremont Peak
articles.summary: This document provides detailed driving directions to Fremont Peak State Park, located south of San Juan Bautista. It outlines the route from Hwy. 101 near Gilroy, including specific turns, distances, and a warning about a road jog, also mentioning a $3 entrance fee.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program Status
articles.summary: This article provides an update on the Telescope Loaner Program, stating that all telescopes are currently available for use. SJAA members interested in borrowing a scope are instructed to contact Mike Koop via email or phone.

articles.title: Current Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes currently loaned out to members, detailing each scope's description, the borrower's name, and the due date. It also informs interested individuals that they can join a waiting list for a scope once it becomes available.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes with extended loan periods, available for borrowing. Interested individuals can request to borrow one of these scopes, and the organization will coordinate a transfer time with the current borrower. The list includes various telescope types, current borrowers, and their due dates.

articles.title: Stored Scopes
articles.summary: The article lists astronomical telescopes available for immediate loan to SJAA members, stored at various members' homes. Members interested in borrowing a scope are instructed to contact Mike Koop for pickup at SJAA events. The list includes details like scope type, size, and who is storing it, along with a note about a recent donation and a request for more storage volunteers.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: The SJAA Ephemeris, the official newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association, is published monthly, totaling 12 issues per year, from January through December. This statement also includes the association's mailing address.

articles.title: To Subscribe to/Unsubscribe from the SJAA Mailing List send email to
articles.summary: This document provides instructions on how to subscribe to or unsubscribe from the SJAA mailing list. Users are directed to send an email to sjaa-request@seds.org with a blank subject line and a body containing either "subscribe" or "unsubscribe." This information is dated August 1998 and is sourced from the SJAA EPHEMERIS.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing membership options for new or renewing members, including standard and junior rates, and an optional Sky & Telescope subscription. It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment (checks payable to SJAA) to the treasurer, Bob Elsberry, either in person at a meeting or via mail. The form also includes contact information fields for the applicant.
